bull_bear.body: Dividend: INR51/share (82% increase); Captive Finance: INR700cr total equity commitment (INR200cr done, INR500cr over next 12-15 months); Greenfield expansion.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical supply chain disruption; Sub-normal monsoon forecast impacting H2 FY27 demand; Permanent labor/energy cost inflation; Cyclical tractor industry correction (alternating growth/de-growth pattern).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic on long-term fundamentals; Pragmatic on near-term cost pressures; Confident in product pipeline offsetting industry flattishness; Disciplined on capital deployment.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Tractor industry exhibits a strict alternating growth/de-growth cycle over 8 years (except FY26 anomaly); Mini excavators currently fully imported from Japan until new plant commissioning; Captive finance ROE target modest (1.5-2%) primarily to drive core volume/market share rather than standalone profit.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Portfolio pruning and asset monetisation: Q1FY26 “included the divestment of the RED business, as well as an exceptional gain from the sale of land and building”, which the deck says makes Q1FY27 reported PAT not directly comparable with Q1FY26 (RED = Railway Equipment).
- A captive financing arm sits in the group — “Escorts Kubota Finance Limited” appears in the company-overview slide and “EKFL Captive Finance” in the milestone timeline.
- Q1FY27 standalone annualised return metrics quoted are ROCE 15.8% and ROE 12.3%; note the deck's own glossary defines ROE as “PAT divided by Average capital employed” (not average equity), so the label and definition disagree.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Three-brand architecture (Farmtrac, Powertrac, Kubota) enabling differentiated positioning across diverse customer segments and geographies
- Deep strategic partnership with Kubota Corporation, Japan providing shared engineering, joint product development, cross-border R&D collaboration and access to Kubota's global distribution network (~60% of export volumes routed through it)
- Captive finance subsidiary Escorts Kubota Finance Limited (EKFL), plus deepened bank/NBFC tie-ups, improving credit access and retail conversion for dealers/customers
- Market leadership in pick-and-carry cranes (41.4% share) and a strengthening position in mini-excavators (19.5% share) within Construction Equipment
- Wide dealer and service network providing last-mile connectivity and after-sales support across agri-machinery and construction equipment
- Conservative, low-leverage balance sheet (debt-equity ratio near zero) supporting a self-sustaining growth model and flexibility to pursue growth opportunities
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material availability and pricing — Management flags the availability and pricing of raw materials as a key factor that could impact operations; elevated input costs in raw materials and traded goods partially offset EBITDA gains in FY26 despite operational leverage and improved product mix.
- Cyclical, rural-income-linked demand in Agri Machinery — Company performance going forward is stated to be shaped by rural demand trends and agricultural income cycles, and MD&A flags 'cyclical demand and pricing in the Company's main markets' as a risk to operations.
- Dependence on infrastructure/public capex momentum in Construction Equipment — The Construction Equipment segment's demand is tied to sustained infrastructure activity and continued public capital expenditure in roads, railways and urban infrastructure; the AR notes 'some variability was observed in project execution timelines' during the year, and Construction Equipment EBIT margin fell to 7.9% from 9.9% the prior year, reflecting margin pressure.
- Regulatory and tax policy changes — MD&A cites changes in government regulations and tax policies as a factor that could impact the Company's operations.
- Global macroeconomic and trade conditions — Outlook explicitly lists global macroeconomic and trade conditions, and economic developments in India and other countries where the Company operates, as factors shaping future performance.
- Near-term earnings visibility reliant on external factors — Company states that 'while near-term visibility relies on external factors,' sustained performance depends on its balance sheet strength, diversified portfolio and operational efficiency rather than assured demand conditions.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Agri Machinery: Rev INR9,710cr (+15.8%), EBIT Margin 12.6% (+190bps); Construction Equipment: Vol 5,794 units (-10.6% YoY), Q4 Rev +22.6%, Margin 12.7% (+386bps).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Two reported segments, with Agri Machinery Products dominant: segmental contribution to total operating revenue of 87% (Q1FY27), 88% (Q1FY26) and 81% (Q4FY26), Construction Equipment being 13% / 12% / 19% respectively.
- Deck traces the company to “1944 Escorts Inception” and lists milestones including “Strategic partnership with Kubota Corporation”, “EKFL Captive Finance”, “One EKL” and “Products Expansion”; the extraction separates the milestone labels from the year labels, so the year-to-milestone binding is lost and individual dates are not asserted here.
- Tractor share of market rises but export share falls: domestic “Share of Market” 10.1% in Q1FY26 to 10.5% in Q1FY27, while export share moves 6.8% to 4.7%.
- Construction Equipment share of market (as per ICEMA) in Q1FY27 is concentrated in cranes: PNC SOM 38.3%, Mini Excavator SOM 17.7%, Compactor SOM 0.5%, BHL SOM 0.5%.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Shareholding] Promoter holding is flat at 68.04% across June'2025 through June'2026, while institutions (FPI/FI/banks/insurers/QIB/AIF) rose 16.65% to 17.85% and public fell 13.64% to 12.45%; non-promoter non-public is 1.65%.
- [Certification] The cover slide carries a “Great Place To Work® Certified JAN 2026-JAN 2027, INDIA” mark.
- [Segment ROCE anomaly] Construction Equipment annualised ROCE is stated as 1357.5% in Q1FY27, an implausibly large figure reproduced verbatim from the deck without reconciliation.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: The Company is primarily engaged in manufacturing, sales, marketing, trading and customer support of Agri-machinery Products (Tractors, Harvesters, Engines, Implements, Spare parts, Oils Lubes etc.) and Construction Equipment Products (Material Handling Cranes, Road Compaction and Earth moving equipment's, Spare parts etc.). It serves a diverse customer base across the agricultural value chain (small and marginal farmers, large farm owners, FPOs, cooperatives, rural entrepreneurs and institutional customers) and across infrastructure and industrial development (construction and engineering companies, government/PSU agencies, mining operators, rental and leasing companies, and individual contractors), with products marketed under the Kubota, Farmtrac, Powertrac, Escorts, Steeltrac, Farmpower and E Kubota brands.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Agri Machinery:** Tractors (Kubota, Farmtrac, Powertrac, Escorts, Steeltrac, Farmpower, E Kubota brands), Harvesters, Rice transplanters (KA6, KA8 ride-on transplanters), Half-feed combines, Farm implements, Engines, Spare parts, Oils & lubricants
- **Construction Equipment:** Material handling cranes (pick-and-carry, Escorts and Kubota brands), Road compaction machinery, Earthmoving equipment (e.g. BLX 75 backhoe loader)

latest_quarter.body: EBIT margin pressure from 5-6% input cost inflation (Steel +7-8%, Tires +15-20%, Energy/Labor permanent hikes); Mitigated by 1.5% price hike in April and product mix improvement.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Flattish to +2/-3% for Tractor Industry in FY27; Margin: Effort to maintain full-year margins despite 5-6% input cost pressure; Order Inflow: Construction equipment seeing sequential recovery; Capex: INR350-400cr normal + INR500cr initial greenfield outlay.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Construction equipment Q4 volume +9% YoY (vs industry +4%); Tractor exports +33.8% YoY; Agri Solutions growing 20%+ CAGR expected.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Greenfield facility (INR5,000cr over 7-10 years); Component exports to Kubota Global (target INR500-1,000cr by FY30); Mini excavator market 3x by 2030; Captive finance AUM scaling.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Strengthen market share across key geographies and customer segments in Agri Machinery while expanding export volumes through Kubota-led international channels
- Scale the Agri Solutions business through wider adoption of implements, harvesting solutions and precision farming equipment
- Expand the Engine business by deepening OEM relationships and addressing demand across agriculture, infrastructure and allied sectors
- Increase the contribution of Service & Spare Parts through deeper aftermarket penetration, enhanced service reach and higher customer engagement
- Capture cross-selling opportunities across tractors, Agri Solutions, engines and spare parts/services to create a comprehensive farm mechanisation ecosystem
- In Construction Equipment, consolidate leadership position in the pick-and-carry crane segment while selectively strengthening presence in mini excavators and application-focused equipment categories
- Sharpen focus on application-led solutions that improve productivity, reliability and operating efficiency for customers across diverse end-use segments
- Improve capacity utilisation, cost absorption and operational efficiencies in Construction Equipment to support profitability and business resilience
- Progress the greenfield manufacturing facility in Uttar Pradesh to significantly enhance production capabilities and support future demand growth
- Align product portfolio with evolving industry dynamics through continued innovation, including exploration of alternative fuel initiatives, to support more efficient and sustainable construction practices
- Dividend decisions are put to shareholder approval at the AGM under a formal Dividend Distribution Policy: at the 80th AGM, shareholders were asked to declare a final dividend and confirm a special dividend already paid during the year for FY 2025-26, reflecting a stated commitment to shareholder value creation. The Company also reinvests in strategic growth via downstream investment into its wholly-owned captive finance subsidiary Escorts Kubota Finance Limited (EKFL), having subscribed to equity shares offered under a rights issue by EKFL during FY 2025-26. Governance policies include a Board Diversity Policy, a Policy for Determining Material Subsidiaries, and a Policy on Materiality of Related Party Transactions, with related-party dealings (including with Kubota Corporation, the holding company) conducted in the ordinary course of business and on an arm's-length basis.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company references an ongoing greenfield expansion project as a core strategic priority, alongside its existing plant network, without stating a rupee quantum or specific location/timeline in this bundle. Management states its priorities remain 'disciplined execution of the three-brand strategy, timely and efficient completion of the greenfield project, deeper integration with Kubota, expansion of non-tractor revenues, and building a focused, segment-leading construction equipment business,' and separately notes that 'our greenfield capacity, combined with Kubota's global network, positions us well to participate competitively and capture future opportunities at scale,' and that the greenfield expansion is expected to create 'thousands of sustainable livelihoods.'
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Company performance going forward will continue to be shaped by rural demand trends and agricultural income cycles, infrastructure investment momentum, commodity price movements, and global macroeconomic and trade conditions
- Agri Machinery segment continues to benefit from long-term structural drivers, including increasing mechanisation of agriculture, the need for improved productivity and a gradual shift towards higher-horsepower tractors
- Infrastructure-led demand continues to remain a key structural driver for the Construction Equipment segment, particularly across government-led capital expenditure programs
- Government of India's sustained infrastructure push, supported by rising government capital expenditure, is driving strong demand in the construction equipment sector, alongside increasing focus on automation, precision-led execution and low-emission machinery
- The Indian tractor industry is evolving rapidly, driven by technology integration, alternative fuel solutions, improved rural financing, and the rise of precision agriculture, reshaping mechanisation and farm productivity
- Agriculture is increasingly impacted by climate factors such as monsoon variability, soil health challenges and land-use changes, highlighting the need for resilient solutions
- Company's strong balance sheet, diversified product portfolio, and continued focus on operational efficiency are expected to support sustained performance over the medium term despite mixed near-term demand visibility
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Escorts Kubota delivered record FY26 volumes and margins driven by a 23% industry boom and product portfolio refresh, but faces a flattish FY27 tractor outlook and significant input cost headwinds (5-6%) from geopolitical tensions. The strategic pivot to a INR5,000cr greenfield expansion and aggressive captive finance infusion (INR700cr total) aims to secure long-term market share despite near-term cyclical moderation.

risks.note: The Construction Equipment segment's demand is tied to sustained infrastructure activity and continued public capital expenditure in roads, railways and urban infrastructure; the AR notes 'some variability was observed in project execution timelines' during the year, and Construction Equipment EBIT margin fell to 7.9% from 9.9% the prior year, reflecting margin pressure.
MD&A cites changes in government regulations and tax policies as a factor that could impact the Company's operations.
Outlook explicitly lists global macroeconomic and trade conditions, and economic developments in India and other countries where the Company operates, as factors shaping future performance.

risks.risk: Near-term earnings visibility reliant on external factors
risks.note: Company states that 'while near-term visibility relies on external factors,' sustained performance depends on its balance sheet strength, diversified portfolio and operational efficiency rather than assured demand conditions.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Escorts Kubota Limited is a leading Indian manufacturer and marketer of agri-machinery (tractors, harvesters, implements) and construction equipment (cranes, compaction and earthmoving machinery), operating under a deep strategic partnership with Kubota Corporation, Japan that channels India into …

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company is primarily engaged in manufacturing, sales, marketing, trading and customer support of Agri-machinery Products (Tractors, Harvesters, Engines, Implements, Spare parts, Oils Lubes etc.) and Construction Equipment Products (Material Handling Cranes, Road Compaction and Earth moving equipment's, Spare parts etc.). It serves a diverse customer base across the agricultural value chain (small and marginal farmers, large farm owners, FPOs, cooperatives, rural entrepreneurs and institutional customers) and across infrastructure and industrial development (construction and engineering companies, government/PSU agencies, mining operators, rental and leasing companies, and individual contractors), with products marketed under the Kubota, Farmtrac, Powertrac, Escorts, Steeltrac, Farmpower and E Kubota brands.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Invigorated Business Consulting Limited — subsidiary: 67.87% shareholding; subsidiary since October 12, 2012
- Farmtrac Tractors Europe Sp. Z.o.o, Poland — subsidiary: 100% shareholding; subsidiary since October 08, 2009
- Escorts Crop Solutions Limited — subsidiary: 100% shareholding; subsidiary since October 12, 2012
- Escorts Benefit and Welfare Trust — subsidiary: 100% shareholding; subsidiary since February 14, 2012
- Escorts Benefit Trust — subsidiary: 100% shareholding; subsidiary since March 04, 2013; liquidated/sold during the year w.e.f. December 18, 2025
- Escorts Kubota Finance Limited (EKFL) — subsidiary: 100% shareholding (wholly-owned); subsidiary since January 09, 2024; the Company's captive finance subsidiary; Company made a downstream investment via rights issue during the year to subscribe equity shares
- EKL CSR Foundation — subsidiary: 100% shareholding; subsidiary since November 01, 2021
- Adico Escorts Agri Equipments Private Limited — JV: Joint venture agreement; 40% holding; associated since April 01, 2015
- Escorts Consumer Credit Limited — associate: 29.41% holding; associated since October 12, 2012
- Kubota Corporation, Japan — related party: Joint Promoter of the Company as equity investor, described as holding company in the related-party transactions note; the only related-party transaction during the year considered material was with Kubota Corporation, approved by shareholders at the last AGM

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Agri Machinery: Rev INR9,710cr (+15.8%), EBIT Margin 12.6% (+190bps); Construction Equipment: Vol 5,794 units (-10.6% YoY), Q4 Rev +22.6%, Margin 12.7% (+386bps).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Agri Machinery:** Tractors (Kubota, Farmtrac, Powertrac, Escorts, Steeltrac, Farmpower, E Kubota brands), Harvesters, Rice transplanters (KA6, KA8 ride-on transplanters), Half-feed combines, Farm implements, Engines, Spare parts, Oils & lubricants
- **Construction Equipment:** Material handling cranes (pick-and-carry, Escorts and Kubota brands), Road compaction machinery, Earthmoving equipment (e.g. BLX 75 backhoe loader)

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic India - 28 states and 8 Union Territories
- International agri-machinery markets - more than 60 countries
- International construction-equipment markets - more than 30 countries
- Exports ~5.54% of total turnover
- ~60% of export volumes routed through Kubota's global distribution network

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Construction equipment Q4 volume +9% YoY (vs industry +4%); Tractor exports +33.8% YoY; Agri Solutions growing 20%+ CAGR expected.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue Growth: Flattish to +2/-3% for Tractor Industry in FY27; Margin: Effort to maintain full-year margins despite 5-6% input cost pressure; Order Inflow: Construction equipment seeing sequential recovery; Capex: INR350-400cr normal + INR500cr initial greenfield outlay.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Greenfield facility (INR5,000cr over 7-10 years); Component exports to Kubota Global (target INR500-1,000cr by FY30); Mini excavator market 3x by 2030; Captive finance AUM scaling.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Company performance going forward will continue to be shaped by rural demand trends and agricultural income cycles, infrastructure investment momentum, commodity price movements, and global macroeconomic and trade conditions
- Agri Machinery segment continues to benefit from long-term structural drivers, including increasing mechanisation of agriculture, the need for improved productivity and a gradual shift towards higher-horsepower tractors
- Infrastructure-led demand continues to remain a key structural driver for the Construction Equipment segment, particularly across government-led capital expenditure programs
- Government of India's sustained infrastructure push, supported by rising government capital expenditure, is driving strong demand in the construction equipment sector, alongside increasing focus on automation, precision-led execution and low-emission machinery
- The Indian tractor industry is evolving rapidly, driven by technology integration, alternative fuel solutions, improved rural financing, and the rise of precision agriculture, reshaping mechanisation and farm productivity
- Agriculture is increasingly impacted by climate factors such as monsoon variability, soil health challenges and land-use changes, highlighting the need for resilient solutions
- Company's strong balance sheet, diversified product portfolio, and continued focus on operational efficiency are expected to support sustained performance over the medium term despite mixed near-term demand visibility

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBIT margin pressure from 5-6% input cost inflation (Steel +7-8%, Tires +15-20%, Energy/Labor permanent hikes); Mitigated by 1.5% price hike in April and product mix improvement.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Dividend: INR51/share (82% increase); Captive Finance: INR700cr total equity commitment (INR200cr done, INR500cr over next 12-15 months); Greenfield expansion.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company references an ongoing greenfield expansion project as a core strategic priority, alongside its existing plant network, without stating a rupee quantum or specific location/timeline in this bundle. Management states its priorities remain 'disciplined execution of the three-brand strategy, timely and efficient completion of the greenfield project, deeper integration with Kubota, expansion of non-tractor revenues, and building a focused, segment-leading construction equipment business,' and separately notes that 'our greenfield capacity, combined with Kubota's global network, positions us well to participate competitively and capture future opportunities at scale,' and that the greenfield expansion is expected to create 'thousands of sustainable livelihoods.'

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic on long-term fundamentals; Pragmatic on near-term cost pressures; Confident in product pipeline offsetting industry flattishness; Disciplined on capital deployment.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Three-brand architecture (Farmtrac, Powertrac, Kubota) enabling differentiated positioning across diverse customer segments and geographies
- Deep strategic partnership with Kubota Corporation, Japan providing shared engineering, joint product development, cross-border R&D collaboration and access to Kubota's global distribution network (~60% of export volumes routed through it)
- Captive finance subsidiary Escorts Kubota Finance Limited (EKFL), plus deepened bank/NBFC tie-ups, improving credit access and retail conversion for dealers/customers
- Market leadership in pick-and-carry cranes (41.4% share) and a strengthening position in mini-excavators (19.5% share) within Construction Equipment
- Wide dealer and service network providing last-mile connectivity and after-sales support across agri-machinery and construction equipment
- Conservative, low-leverage balance sheet (debt-equity ratio near zero) supporting a self-sustaining growth model and flexibility to pursue growth opportunities

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Geopolitical supply chain disruption; Sub-normal monsoon forecast impacting H2 FY27 demand; Permanent labor/energy cost inflation; Cyclical tractor industry correction (alternating growth/de-growth pattern).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Tractor industry exhibits a strict alternating growth/de-growth cycle over 8 years (except FY26 anomaly); Mini excavators currently fully imported from Japan until new plant commissioning; Captive finance ROE target modest (1.5-2%) primarily to drive core volume/market share rather than standalone profit.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen market share across key geographies and customer segments in Agri Machinery while expanding export volumes through Kubota-led international channels
- Scale the Agri Solutions business through wider adoption of implements, harvesting solutions and precision farming equipment
- Expand the Engine business by deepening OEM relationships and addressing demand across agriculture, infrastructure and allied sectors
- Increase the contribution of Service & Spare Parts through deeper aftermarket penetration, enhanced service reach and higher customer engagement
- Capture cross-selling opportunities …

other.body:

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.
